messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from today's authz incident postmortem. Root cause was missing audience check in the internal service token validation, which allowed stale tokens minted for service A to access service B's read endpoints. Summary + action items below.

toni: ack. thanks for running the postmortem. can we get owners and due dates?

sam: assigning myself to token validation fix (add audience + stricter exp checks). Plan: patch runtime lib, deploy canary, monitor 48h. ETA: 2024-06-30.

maya: @sam please also add an automated unit + integration test that runs a token with wrong aud and expects 401. Add to CI gating.

sam: will do. test in authz-lib + e2e in staging.

irina: I'm taking permissions review for all service-to-service read scopes. Goal: map endpoints -> required roles, identify any broad scopes. ETA: 2024-07-07.

derick: I'll handle audit logging gaps. Noticed missing role-change entries between 2024-05-10 and 2024-05-12 in the logs; need to ensure service account role assignments are logged and immutable. Action: enable detailed audit for IAM mutations, pipe to longterm storage, and add alert on missing audit heartbeats. ETA: 2024-07-05.

maya: secrets rotation follow-up: rotate all long-lived service tokens older than 90 days, and add TTL enforcement for issued tokens. Who owns rotation ops?

toni: infra will run rotation ops. I'll own the runbook and the automation. Breaking into two steps: (1) rotate tokens for low-risk services (canary) by 2024-06-28, (2) full roll by 2024-07-12.

sam: note — some clients still depend on the old audience behavior. I'll coordinate a compatibility flag in authz-lib and communicate in #eng-runtime before canary.

irina: re recurring pattern: we saw similar token-aud failure in Feb where a deployment skipped env var AUD_OVERRIDE. Suggest we add a weekly audit job that samples token validations across environments and fails CI if mismatch rate > 0.1%.

derick: log grep I used to find missing role logs: `grep -R "role_change" /var/log/audit/ | sed -n '1,200p'` — moving that into an automated check.

maya: created follow-up epic: INFSEC-2143 (service-token-hardening). @audit-bot please create tasks for each owner and link PRs.

audit-bot: Created Jira tasks: INFSEC-2144 (token validation tests) -> sam; INFSEC-2145 (permissions audit) -> irina; INFSEC-2146 (audit log hardening) -> derick; INFSEC-2147 (secrets rotation runbook + automation) -> toni. Rules: include SLA and rollback plan.

toni: putting runbook draft in /docs/runbooks/service-token-rotation.md and will link PR in the ticket.

sam: quick acceptance criteria for my change: 1) unit + e2e tests; 2) canary deploy shows 0 auth regressions for 48h; 3) perf overhead < 3% token validation latency.

irina: permissions review acceptance: list of endpoints with tightened scopes + roll plan for impacted teams.

maya: please update the postmortem doc with these action items and owners. I'll check in during next incident retro. Recurring incident tracking: we'll add a monthly authz incident trend to the incident dashboard.

toni: noted. I'll add alerting for elevated cross-service read failures (rate >0.05% of calls) and include it in the dashboard.

sam: will open draft PR today for token validation change and link INFSEC-2144.

maya: thanks all — small follow-ups: include changelog entries, communicate to #customers if any maintenance windows needed, and set an audit review meeting next Wednesday.

derick: adding a small retention policy note: once audit logs are in longterm storage we should ship a monthly diff report to security@redwood.com.

maya: perfect. I'll close the postmortem checklists once all PRs merged and runbook published.

toni: :thumbsup:

sam: confirming ETA and will ping if any blockers.

irina: will reach out to the teams with potential scope breaks before 2024-07-07.

maya: end of thread — keeping this open until INFSEC-2143 is marked resolved.
